newsitem.title: USA: Entergy sees few Ark. power flow snags after storm.
newsitem.headline: Entergy sees few Ark. power flow snags after storm.

text.p: Entergy Corp said Tuesday extensive tornado damage to its Arkansas transmission system was hampering the flow of electricity into its service territory but was not impeding the regional power market.
"Our system operating center says the transmission problems have mostly affected moving power into our area from the north," said Carol Copeland, spokeswoman at Entergy's Little Rock, Ark., office.
"But there is no indication of large demand (in the region) or a need to move power north," she said, citing mild weather and light loads on the system.

Copeland said the company had restored two 115 kilovolt (kv) lines near Little Rock, Ark., but that most of the big transmission lines snapped by a series of tornadoes this past weekend were still down.

The severe weather, part of a late winter storm that is blamed for 48 deaths from Texas to Pennsylvania, damaged or destroyed 36 steel towers supporting five of Entergy's 500 kv transmission lines in Arkansas.
"The 500 kv lines are still down. They are still working on replacing their concrete foundations," Copeland said.
She said another six 161 kv lines and four 115 kv lines were also still down.
The company estimated Monday it could take up to three weeks to restore all the damaged transmission lines.

Local power distribution was faring somewhat better, with only about 300 customers still without power. This number does not include customers whose homes or businesses were so badly damaged that they are unable to receive power.
Some 18,000 of Entergy's 611,000 customers in Arkansas were without power this past weekend after a series of tornadoes cut a 250-mile path across the state.
New Orleans-based Entergy maintains about 119,000 miles of transmission and distribution lines in its service territory, which covers parts of Louisiana, Arkansas, Mississippi, and eastern Texas.
